title: BRUE Pathway
sources: AAP 2016 Clinical Practice Guideline (Tieder JS et al. Pediatrics 2016;137(5):e20160590)
Brooks AF et al. Pediatrics 2019;144(2):e20184101 (higher-risk framework)

changelog.change: Initial entry — lower-risk pathway matches AAP 2016 exactly; higher-risk side is a stub pending the 2019 framework.

purpose: Classify an infant event as a BRUE, then stratify lower- vs higher-risk to guide testing and disposition.

body.text: An episode in an infant < 1 year, lasting < 1 minute (typically 20-30 s), with ≥ 1 of: cyanosis or pallor; absent, decreased, or irregular breathing; marked change in tone (hyper- or hypotonia); altered responsiveness — AND no explanation found after a full history and exam. If there is an explanation (e.g. GERD, choking, infection), it is not a BRUE — work up the cause.

items: Gestational age ≥ 32 weeks AND corrected gestational age ≥ 45 weeks
No CPR by a trained medical provider
No concerning history or physical exam findings

body.text: Lower-risk: brief monitoring (continuous pulse oximetry + serial observation), parental education on BRUE and CPR, shared decision-making. Do NOT routinely obtain labs, imaging, admission, or home monitors. May consider a 12-lead ECG and pertussis testing.

STUB. The 2016 AAP guideline does not cover the higher-risk infant. Build this branch from Brooks AF et al. Pediatrics 2019;144(2):e20184101 — a tiered framework — rather than improvising. Default until then: admission with workup guided by the specific concerning features present.

buildNote: Lower-risk pathway is safe to build now. Higher-risk branch needs the 2019 paper (listed in docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md).
